primary_diagnosis_treated: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease with recent STEMI and HFrEF in the context of stage 5 CKD
nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (IHD) and NG106 (Chronic heart failure) and NG203 (CKD)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2 weeks to target 10 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Cardioprotective ACE‑I for secondary prevention of IHD, HFrEF disease‑modifying therapy and reduction of proteinuria in CKD
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 ACE‑I recommended for all IHD patients; NG106 first‑line for HFrEF; NG203 ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (adjust up to 80 mg BID based on weight, edema and urine output)
medications.duration: Start now, titrate to symptom control, then Lifelong — review annually
medications.purpose: Relieve volume overload in HFrEF and control hypertension in CKD stage 5
medications.nice_justification: NG106 loop diuretic for fluid overload in heart failure

medications.dose: 12.5 mg orally twice daily (target 25 mg BID if tolerated, titrate every 2 weeks)
medications.duration: Lifelong — titrate to HR <70 bpm and SBP >110 mmHg
medications.purpose: Disease‑modifying beta‑blocker for HFrEF and post‑MI angina control
medications.nice_justification: NG106 beta‑blocker for HFrEF; CG126 beta‑blocker for angina symptom control

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of recurrent myocardial infarction
Dual antiplatelet therapy for recent ACS
medications.nice_justification: NG185 DAPT for 12 months after STEMI

medications.purpose: Intensive lipid‑lowering to reduce cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: CG126 high‑intensity statin for all IHD patients

medications.purpose: Blood pressure control in CKD and hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 ACE‑I/ARB first‑line for CKD hypertension; thiazide as adjunct when BP uncontrolled

medications.dose: 21 mg/24 h patch (step up from 7 mg/24 h if still smoking)
medications.purpose: Smoking cessation to reduce cardiovascular risk
Management of major depressive disorder, supporting adherence to cardiovascular therapy
medications.nice_justification: Depression treatment improves outcomes in chronic disease (clinical best practice)

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and ARB markedly increase risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, potentially raising carvedilol levels → bradycardia/hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Titrate carvedilol slowly; monitor heart rate and blood pressure; consider switching to bisoprolol if intolerance

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect may cause volume depletion, electrolyte disturbances
interactions_checked.action: Check weight, BP, electrolytes after 3‑5 days; reduce HCTZ dose if over‑diuresis occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: Both potassium‑sparing → high risk of hyperkalaemia in eGFR 10 mL/min
interactions_checked.action: Do not start spironolactone while Losartan is continued; only consider after stopping ARB and confirming K⁺ ≤5 mmol/L

contraindications.reason: Contra‑indicated in combination with ACE‑I (Ramipril) – risk of hyperkalaemia and AKI; also patient has stage 5 CKD
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue Losartan and continue Ramipril as ACE‑I monotherapy

contraindications.reason: High risk of severe hyperkalaemia with eGFR 10 mL/min and concurrent ACE‑I; potassium level unknown
contraindications.alternative: Only consider after confirming serum K⁺ ≤5 mmol/L and after stopping ARB; otherwise avoid

contraindications.reason: eGFR 10 mL/min is below the minimum threshold (≥20 mL/min) for initiation per NICE TA902/TA929
contraindications.alternative: Re‑evaluate if renal function improves to ≥20 mL/min

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 5; NSAIDs accelerate renal decline and increase cardiovascular risk per CG126 and NG106
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol or topical agents for osteoarthritis pain

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium and bicarbonate values are not provided; required before starting ACE‑I, MRA or adjusting diuretics.
Exact time since STEMI is not recorded; DAPT duration assumes patient is within the 12‑month window.
Left ventricular ejection fraction not documented; HFrEF assumption based on recent MI and CKD‑driven myocardial injury.
Patient’s smoking status assumed ongoing because nicotine patch is prescribed; smoking cessation counseling required.
No documented allergy to ACE‑I or statin; assumed none.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril (after stopping losartan) and furosemide for cardioprotection, blood pressure control and volume management; up‑titrate carvedilol to 12.5 mg BID for HFrEF benefit; continue guideline‑recommended antiplatelet, high‑intensity statin, nicotine patch and fluoxetine. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, blood pressure and heart rate closely, especially after each dose change. Avoid ACE‑I + ARB combo, NSAIDs, and SGLT2‑i until eGFR improves. Provide lifestyle advice (smoking cessation, low‑salt diet, weight management) and arrange regular follow‑up.
